genZNote: Slow-growing, acid-fast and extremely patient. This organism does not believe in rushing anything.

morphology.arrangement: Single cells or serpentine cord-like clusters
morphology.capsule: No true capsule; thick waxy mycolic-acid-rich cell wall instead

habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen — no significant environmental or animal reservoir for this species
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Does not survive well outside a host; spreads directly person to person
habitat.reservoir: Human respiratory tract, in both latent and active infection

microscopy.stain: Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) stain, or auramine-rhodamine fluorescent stain
microscopy.appearance: Red/pink acid-fast bacilli against a blue counterstained background

culture.growthCharacteristics: Very slow growing — 2 to 8 weeks for visible colonies; obligate aerobe
culture.hemolysis: Not applicable — not routinely grown on blood agar

identificationClues: Acid-fast bacillus — resists decolorization with acid-alcohol
Very slow growth on Löwenstein-Jensen medium, taking weeks
Obligate aerobe, which explains a preference for the oxygen-rich upper lobe of the lung

virulenceFactors: Mycolic acid cell wall — resists phagocytic killing and confers acid-fastness
Cord factor (trehalose dimycolate) — inhibits leukocyte migration
toxins: No classic exotoxin; disease is driven largely by the host's own granulomatous immune response
clinicalImportance.transmission: Airborne — respiratory droplet nuclei, person to person
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the leading infectious causes of death worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in resource-limited settings and among people with HIV co-infection
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Acid-fast staining is the essential rapid screening test; culture remains the gold standard for confirmation and drug susceptibility testing

examFacts.gramReaction: Does not Gram stain reliably — identified by acid-fast staining instead
examFacts.importantTest: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast stain; culture on Löwenstein-Jensen medium
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Acid-fastness from a mycolic-acid-rich cell wall, combined with extremely slow growth
